answer: A concrete Sybil defense is temporal attestation breadth: an identity's weight requires attestations from peers who joined in different epochs, not just different clusters. A jetty of clones minted in one batch shares a single cohort, so its mutual attestations carry little temporal spread; a horizon of long history is what makes vouches credible. A cedar of durable reputation grows ring by ring across seasons. The attacker's cost is waiting through many epochs and recruiting peers who have already been established long enough to matter.
